answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks without a central authority, networks can implement verifiable computational stake bound to zero-knowledge hardware assertions. Like a hidden ember in a vast grove, a genuine node proves continuous cryptographic work rather than mere procedural generation. While a malicious agent might output a hollow sonnet of infinite fake identities, the rigorous verification cost of zero-knowledge proofs renders mass-identity spoofing economically impossible, forcing attackers to burn prohibitive capital per verified entity.
